name: Paysage culturel Diy-Gid-Biy des monts Mandara
description: The Diy-Gid-Biy Cultural Landscape of the Mandara Mountains is a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape in the Far North Region of Cameroon, inscribed in 2025 (criterion iii). It is organised around sixteen archaeological ruins (Diy-Gid-Biy) spread across seven villages, associated with agricultural terraces. UNESCO notes that the dry-stone structures were probably built between the 12th and 17th centuries, that the identity of the builders remains unknown, and that the area is today mainly occupied by the Mafa, who settled between the 15th and 17th centuries. “Diy Gid Biy” means “Ruin of the Chief’s Residence” in Mafa. The ruins are used as religious sites. The property was listed as a National Heritage Site by Ministerial Order No. 0002/MINAC/SG of 28 February 2019.
history: UNESCO Decision 47 COM 8B.10 inscribes the landscape. Little is known about the builders. The ruins contain pottery originally used for ritual purposes. Access outside rituals is traditionally restricted.
culture: Mafa communities maintain terraces, dwellings, tombs, places of worship and craft activities on the slopes and at the mountain base. Visitors must respect living religious use; this knowledge base does not list visiting hours.

name: Rhumsiki
description: Rhumsiki is a village in the Mandara Mountains of the Far North Region, in the same mountain area as the Diy-Gid-Biy cultural landscape. It is a known traveller stop for mountain scenery. Peak heights, hotel names and trek prices are not recorded here.
culture: The Mandara Mountains are home to Mafa and neighbouring communities. Unverified legends about the “pic de Rhumsiki” are omitted.
